A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HEAPr work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching v1 Appendix A to its revised counterpart in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original HEAPr pruning results, global-versus-layer-wise comparisons, compression/FLOPs curves, and calibration sensitivity experiments. Some baseline results are attributed to prior publications.

after.justification: V2 retains original HEAPr results and adds pruning-granularity experiments, loss/importance comparisons, computational-cost measurements, and layer-wise pruning profiles.

M1.justification: The atomic decomposition, shared gradient covariance, token-averaged importance calculation, and global pruning procedure remain unchanged in Section 3.3 and Algorithm 1. The algorithm's token-index correction aligns it with the existing Equation 16; the revised theoretical derivation does not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Table 1 adds Wiki and PTB evaluations beyond the seven retained zero-shot benchmarks. WikiText-2 already appeared as calibration data in v1. The four evaluated MoE models and WikiText-2/C4 calibration coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: MoE-SVD newly participates in Table 1's DeepSeekMoE-16B-Base comparison at 20% pruning, with average accuracy 0.54. Existing comparators remain in their corresponding comparisons, including CAMERA-P in Table 2. Table 3 also introduces a whole-expert ablation comparator using summed atomic importance scores.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends evaluation design with lower-is-better Wiki/PTB scores, pruning-cost measurements using TFLOPs, GPU time and peak memory, and loss tests on 10% bins ordered by expert index. The retained HEAPr setup still uses 128 sequences of 2048 tokens and LM-Evaluation-Harness 0.4.7; Appendix B's sampling recipe is newly disclosed rather than evidence of a changed existing protocol.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained compression, global-versus-layer-wise, and calibration analyses, v2 tests atomic versus whole-expert pruning in Table 3 and importance-score correspondence with loss in Figure 3. Appendices C and D add computational-overhead comparisons and layer-wise compression profiles under 25% and 50% global pruning. These directly examine the pruning granularity, scoring rationale, and practical behavior.

E5.justification: The calibration plot changes from unaccompanied curves in v1 Figure 3 to curves with uncertainty bands in v2 Figure 4, described as error bars over random calibration subsets. Appendix B newly specifies random.seed(0). Neither the repetition count nor the statistical meaning of the bands is supplied, and an increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: V2 adds Wiki/PTB results, MoE-SVD scores, granularity outcomes, pruning costs, and loss/layer-profile findings. In retained Table 1 settings, HEAPr's Qwen3/25% ARC-E score changes from 0.77 to 0.76 and Qwen2/40% HellaSwag from 0.64 to 0.63. Table 2 scores remain unchanged. Section 4.2 also swaps 55% retained accuracy and 38% FLOPs reduction at 90% pruning, contradicting the retained Figure 2 values.

T1.justification: Appendix A replaces the convergence-based Jacobian-independence argument with explicit conditional expectations over model outputs and an outer expectation over inputs. Section 3.2 reformulates the constraint per token and revises Equations 12–13 to approximate, input-averaged loss expressions. These change the central derivation and its assumptions, beyond notation. The stated CAMERA-P formula also changes its second norm from L2 to L-infinity.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: output-space second-order atomic pruning, reduced storage complexity, two forward passes and one backward pass, and near-lossless pruning around 20–25% for most evaluated models. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly qualifies the importance score as useful for ranking rather than exact loss prediction because higher-order terms are neglected. It adds explanations connecting atomic pruning to computational savings and layer-dependent pruning rates to redundancy. These are substantive but focused extensions of the existing interpretation; Figure 3's inverted loss axis complicates its claimed loss/importance agreement.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds corpus concatenation, tokenization and segment-sampling instructions, model-specific baseline provenance, and calibration budgets, including D2-MoE's 512 samples versus HEAPr's 128. Table 1 marks results obtained from official implementations. Appendix F newly states checkpoint availability alongside the previously supplied code link. These substantially improve documentation, although GPU hardware remains unspecified.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds EEP and describes its evolutionary combination of expert dropping and merging. The broader research positioning remains stable. MoE-SVD receives an explicit comparison role, but its closely matching SVD work was already cited in v1; publication/preprint variants of existing references are not separate research additions.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the abstract, introduction, and conclusion remain intact. V2 edits terminology and local prose, expands the constraint explanation and Appendix A, and adds an appendix roadmap, acknowledgments, and disclosure sections. Affiliations and publication headers also change; the retained narrative is not extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains Wiki/PTB columns, source markers, and revised styling. V2 adds Tables 3–5 and Figures 3, 5, and 6. Figure 2 is redrawn, while the calibration analysis moves from Figure 3 to Figure 4 with a logarithmic sample axis and uncertainty bands. These substantially extend and revise the experimental displays.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility documentation and adds relevant granularity, cost, and scoring analyses. However, new Figure 3 reverses the loss axis: visually aligned curves correspond to opposing numerical trends, leaving its claimed validation unclear. Section 4.2 also introduces the 55%/38% reversal despite unchanged Figure 2 values. These problems affect the interpretation of the added evidence, so the documentation gains and scientific-reporting harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
